clue.text: Calling trick very cheap, powerful girl?

parts.note: a knockdown price is a very low one
Ginger Spice was one of the Spice Girls, whose slogan was 'girl power'

explanation.surface: A cheap trick played by a strong-willed girl.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the British children's prank of knocking on a door and running away before anyone answers; 'Calling' is visiting someone's house, not phoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The prank is a trick played by pretending to call at someone's door, then fleeing.

clue.text: Drink up, last bit of scotch moments away

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: last bit of points to the final letter of scotch

explanation.surface: Someone downs their drink as the whisky runs out, closing time moments away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only moments away is close at hand; the archaic word for near.

clue.text: Crack troops in the end restrained by hero, briefly

indicators.note: restrained by means held inside the shortened word for hero
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a champ, champion, is a hero

indicators.note: in the end picks the last letter of troops

explanation.surface: Troops, in the end, are held back by a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final P of CHAMP to give CHAM, and 'restrained by' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a deep fissure or gap, a synonym in the geological sense.

clue.text: Medic removed lid from metal tube dispensing medicine, say?

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: removed lid from means the top letter of the metal word is taken off

parts.note: copper is a metal

explanation.surface: A doctor unscrews the cap of a metal tube to dispense medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed lid from' takes the first letter off COPPER, leaving OPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette for eye drops or other liquid medicine is an example; the 'say?' signals an example.

clue.text: Carve two little heads in alabaster?

indicators.note: in means those letters go inside the colour word

parts.note: alabaster as an adjective means smooth and white

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the words two and little

explanation.surface: A sculptor carves two small heads in alabaster stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alabaster' looks like the stone being carved, but here it is an adjective for the colour; 'heads' and 'in' then work on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare wood away with a knife is to carve it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: See 23
So described, the devil has to be furious with itself?

indicators.note: to be furious is to be wild and churned up, so the letters of has and itself are mixed

explanation.surface: The devil, so the story goes, rages at itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be furious' rearranges HAS and ITSELF together. The devil is a being without belief in God, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the archetype of disloyalty and unbelief, so describing him as lacking belief fits.

clue.text: Bar one nation, everything held out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: everything held out means all the contents removed, leaving only the outer letters of nation

explanation.surface: A single nation that banishes everything it holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everything held out' empties NATION of its inside letters, leaving N and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub, where drinks are served, is a bar; a tavern or public house.

clue.text: Cheeky couple touring northern city in France

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the cheeks word wraps around N

parts.note: the nates are the buttocks, a pair of cheeks

explanation.surface: A cheeky pair travel round a northern city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky couple' is a pun: the nates are the two cheeks of the bottom. 'touring' puts N inside NATES.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a port city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Most original, a grotesque making things alluring?

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted and misshapen, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: The most original, grotesque art can make things seem alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotesque' rearranges the thirteen letters of MOST ORIGINAL A.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something seem attractive and glamorous is the process the noun describes.

clue.text: Old drink bottles nicked, a drunkard lacking energy knocked over, his features rearranged?

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the old drink wraps the reversed run

parts.note: mead is an old drink made from honey

indicators.note: knocked over means the stolen, a and drinker pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: nicked goods are hot, stolen

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is taken away from the drinker word

parts.note: a toper is a drunkard
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A drunkard downs old drink and stolen bottles, gets knocked over, and his face is rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns the whole run including TOPR (from 'lacking') around, and 'bottles' sets it in the old drink. The toy is a plastic potato whose face parts children rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic Hasbro toy is a plastic tuber whose eyes, nose and mouth plug in anywhere.

clue.text: A good time to squeeze loathsome leader out

indicators.note: to squeeze means the good-time word holds that letter inside it

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity, a good time

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of loathsome

explanation.surface: A good time to force out a loathsome leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives L, which 'to squeeze' puts inside BOOM. 'out' is not an indicator but the definition: flowers that are out are in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out have opened their blossoms, which is being in flower.

clue.text: Bridge accessing industrial town

indicators.note: accessing suggests getting inside the words industrial town, where the letters lie

explanation.surface: A bridge giving access to an industrial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accessing' signals the letters inside indust(RIAL TO)wn.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous arched span over the Grand Canal in Venice is called this.

clue.text: Quick player finding success with national team? Not a lot

parts.note: success is a win

indicators.note: Not means the words for a lot are left out of the national team

parts.note: Germany has a national team
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A quick player finds success with the national side, but not often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a lot' removes MANY from GERMANY, leaving GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide player on the wing in football or rugby is typically the fastest in the side.

clue.text: Famously witty American footballer's aim to tackle flipping dishonest footballer?

indicators.note: to tackle means the aim word takes hold of the reversed cheat inside it

parts.note: a footballer aims for a goal

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the cheat word is read backwards

parts.note: a diver is a footballer who dishonestly falls over to win a foul

explanation.surface: A footballer aims to tackle a cheating opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild British expletive but reverses the cheat, and 'to tackle' encloses it. A diver feigns fouls to win free kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist and essayist was renowned for his barbed wit and epigrams.

clue.text: Wind set to change, too soon for a mask?

indicators.note: for a mask means the too-soon word covers the rearranged letters

parts.note: too soon means early

indicators.note: to change means the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mask worn too soon, perhaps before a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the noun, a breeze, not the verb to twist. 'to change' rearranges set, and 'for a mask' has the early word cover it.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze blowing from the east is named by its direction, a meteorological term.

clue.text: Safe with sparks flying off, perhaps? Case of laser opening it

indicators.note: opening it means the case letters split the burning word, it being that word

parts.note: something giving off sparks is on fire, alight

indicators.note: Case of means the outside letters of laser

explanation.surface: A laser cuts open a safe with sparks flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like the strongbox being cut, but it is the adjective. 'Case of' and 'opening it' put the laser's outside letters into the burning word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unharmed, okay and out of danger is a colloquial synonym for safe.

clue.text: See 1
Trendy top Kate hasn't left for matching outfit

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of Trendy
hasn't left means L, the abbreviation for left, is taken out of the actress's surname

parts.note: Kate Winslet is the English actress

explanation.surface: Kate leaves without her trendy top for a matching outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kate' needs her surname, WINSLET; 'hasn't left' removes L to give WINSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan and jumper knitted to match, worn together, is a classic British women's outfit.

clue.text: See 20
Shift work in bordering state ultimately less stable

indicators.note: Shift means move about, so the letters of work in and the end of state are rearranged together
ultimately picks the last letter of state

explanation.surface: Shift work in a border state makes life less stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E, the end of state, and 'Shift' rearranges it with WORK IN; 'bordering' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wobbly or shaky is more unsteady, a British colloquial comparative.

clue.text: It's generally believed I wasn't in love when messing around — responsibly protected?

indicators.note: protected means the rubber word wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: responsibly protected in sex means wearing a condom

indicators.note: messing around means the letters of I wasn't in love are jumbled

explanation.surface: A casual lover confesses there was no love, only fooling around, but at least with protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsibly protected' suggests safe sex, so the rubber sheath wraps the letters that 'messing around' jumbles from I WASN'T IN LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names ideas widely accepted as true, popular belief that may be unexamined.

clue.text: Language lesson is needed, primarily, before travel

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of lesson, is and needed

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A language lesson is needed before going abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon or foreign speech is called this, an informal word for tongue.

clue.text: Relative extremes of Bognor and Exeter

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of Bognor and of Exeter

explanation.surface: A relative travels between the far-flung towns of Bognor and Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is an English seaside town; Exeter is a city in Devon. The definition is the dialect form used in the Uncle Remus tales, as in Brer Rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect contraction of brother, the sibling, used in African-American folk stories.

clue.text: Remarkably gifted bowler, one on hand to relieve pressure, possibly?

definitions.text: one on hand to relieve pressure, possibly?

indicators.note: Remarkably means in an unusual way, so the letters of gifted are rearranged

parts.note: a spinner is a cricket bowler who spins the ball

explanation.surface: A talented cricket bowler comes on to relieve the pressure on his team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a spinner is a slow bowler who turns the ball. The definition is cryptic: the toy is held on the hand to relieve stress.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm-held spinning gadget is marketed as a stress-relieving toy for restless fingers.

clue.text: Rides here weighted incorrectly, fillies initially ahead

indicators.note: ahead means that letter goes in front of the rest
initially picks the first letter of fillies

parts.note: a contest weighted incorrectly is biased, unjust

explanation.surface: A horse race with the weights wrongly set, with the young mares leading.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a handicap race, but 'Rides' are amusements like dodgems and carousels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgems, carousels and big wheels are the attractions at a travelling amusement park.

clue.text: Only 50% required in examination that's overly detailed

indicators.note: Only 50% required in means just the first half of the examination word is used

parts.note: an analysis is an examination

explanation.surface: Only half marks are needed to pass the exam, which is overly detailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only 50% required' keeps the first four of the eight letters of ANALYSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fussy and obsessive about small details is the informal, Freudian-derived sense.

clue.text: Brilliant poet admitting nothing is right

parts.note: a star is brilliant, shining

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the poet word holds the zero letter

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A brilliant poet admits that nothing is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is the definition, the nautical side, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the right-hand side when facing forward has this nautical name.
